meta.name: Generate structured drama scripts from webhook requests using OpenAI and Google Sheets

name: Generate complete drama scripts with AI from topic and genre via webhook

parameters.content:
## Generate complete drama scripts with AI from topic and genre via webhook

This workflow turns a simple topic and genre into a complete, production-ready drama script — characters, act and scene breakdowns, full dialogue with stage directions, emotional beats, themes, and production notes — all returned as structured JSON via webhook.

### Who's it for
- Screenwriters and playwrights who want a fast first draft to react to and revise
- Theatre groups, film students, and content creators needing rapid script prototypes
- Apps or bots that need on-demand scripted content (interactive fiction, training scenarios, roleplay content)
- Writers' rooms looking for brainstorm material or alternate scene takes

### How it works
1. Caller sends a POST request with a topic, genre, and optional act count/tone
2. Code validates the input and maps the genre to tone, pacing, and style guidelines
3. AI generates a story outline: title, logline, themes, full character profiles, and an act/scene breakdown
4. AI expands that outline into a complete script — full dialogue and stage directions per scene, with emotional beats noted
5. AI generates production notes: staging, lighting/sound ideas, costume/set direction, casting notes, runtime estimate
6. Everything is merged into one structured JSON object
7. The request is logged to Google Sheets for tracking
8. Webhook returns the complete script as JSON to the caller

### How to set up
1. Import this workflow into n8n
2. Add your OpenAI credentials to all three OpenAI Chat Model nodes
3. Add Google Sheets OAuth2 credentials and replace YOUR_SHEET_ID in the logging node
4. Activate the workflow and POST a test request with topic, genre, numberOfActs, and tone

### Requirements
- OpenAI API key (GPT-4.1 or above recommended for long-form dialogue)
- Google Sheets with OAuth2 credentials (optional, for logging)

### How to customize
- Adjust genre style guidelines in Code - Validate & Configure Genre Style
- Change default act/scene counts per genre
- Swap the three-stage AI pipeline for a single mega-prompt if you prefer fewer tokens/lower cost
- Add a fourth AI stage for a cold open / teaser scene
- Swap Google Sheets logging for Airtable or Notion
- Add a translation step to deliver scripts in other languages

### Google Sheets Column Layout
Set up your ScriptRequests tab with these headers in row 1:
Request ID | Date | Timestamp | Topic | Genre | Title | Number Of Acts | Number Of Scenes | Word Count | Status

## 1. Trigger & Input Validation

Accepts script requests via webhook POST.

Required POST fields: topic, genre. Optional: numberOfActs (default 3), tone (default matches genre), targetLength (short / medium / full-length).

The Set node normalizes all fields and generates a unique requestId and timestamp.

The Code node maps the genre to a set of style guidelines (tone descriptors, pacing notes, typical scene count) and clamps numberOfActs to a sane range (1–5).

If topic or genre is missing, the Filter routes to an error handler that immediately returns a clear error response to the caller instead of calling the AI.

## 2. Outline & Character Generation

The first AI stage takes the topic, genre, and style guidelines and produces the creative blueprint for the whole script:

- Title and one-line logline
- Core themes
- Setting
- Full character profiles (name, role, age, description, want vs. need, arc)
- Act-by-act, scene-by-scene breakdown with a short summary and emotional beat for each scene

The AI is instructed to respond with JSON only, which the following Code node parses safely (falling back gracefully if the model wraps the JSON in text or code fences).

## 3. Full Script Expansion

The second AI stage takes the parsed outline (characters + act/scene breakdown) and writes the actual script.

For every scene it produces:
- A scene heading and location
- Full stage directions
- Complete character dialogue, line by line, with any parenthetical actor direction
- A short note on the emotional beat being played

The model is instructed to keep every character's voice consistent with their profile from stage one, and to return everything as structured JSON so it can be merged programmatically later rather than left as loose prose.

## 4. Production Notes, Merge & Delivery

The third AI stage adds a director's-eye layer on top of the finished script: staging suggestions, lighting/sound design ideas, costume and set notes, casting suggestions, an estimated runtime, and any content notes worth flagging.

Code - Format Final Script Output merges the outline, full script, and production notes into a single JSON object and computes basic stats like total scene count and word count.

Log to Google Sheet Tracker appends one audit row per request (continueOnFail is on, so a Sheets outage never blocks the response).

Webhook Response - Send Script returns the complete script package as JSON to the original caller.
